expanded_source_wording_tex:
We state the perimeter once, here, and again in \S\ref{sec:scope}. We do \emph{not} derive
$\mathsf{ZF}$ or $\mathsf{ZFC}$ from finite principles; the infinitary content enters only
through the priced assumption box. We prove \emph{no} consistency statement, relative or
absolute, beyond what we explicitly import. We claim \emph{no} new independence result; the
forcing section reorganizes classical theorems, it does not reprove or extend them. We do
\emph{not} claim that $\mathsf{ZFC}$ is the unique or most natural promoted set layer---the
continuum-hypothesis instance is precisely an argument that it is not. And the reading of all
this as an answer to ``where does mathematics come from,'' developed in
\S\ref{sec:discussion}, is offered at the grade of discussion, after the theorems, never as
one of them.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What we do \emph{not} claim.}
\begin{enumerate}\itemsep0pt
  \item We do not derive $\mathsf{ZF}$ or $\mathsf{ZFC}$ from finite principles. The infinitary
  content enters only through the priced assumption box; the four commitments are named
  hypotheses, never conclusions.
  \item We prove no consistency statement, relative or absolute, beyond the classical results we
  explicitly import. Nothing here bears on the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.
  \item We claim no new independence result. The forcing section reorganizes classical theorems
  into the framework's vocabulary; it reproves and extends nothing. No model is constructed.
  \item We do not claim $\mathsf{ZFC}$ is the unique or most natural promoted set layer. The
  continuum-hypothesis instance (\S\ref{sec:ch}) is an argument to the contrary, and structural or
  alternative set theories remain available.
  \item We make no metaphysical claim about the existence of a set-theoretic universe. ``Set'' is
  used as a package; ``$\in$'' as a lens; the readings are structural.
  \item The interpretation of all this as an account of where mathematics comes from
  (\S\ref{sec:discussion}) is offered at the grade of discussion (\gradetag{meta}), after the theorems, and
  is never used as a premise for any of them.
\end{enumerate}
